open_obligations: Note that Wen et al.'s levels are pairwise comparisons, whereas Saunders et al.'s critique task asks for a flaw to be pointed out and their discrimination tasks are binary.
Check whether Saunders et al.'s helpfulness task is a first instance of critique-of-critique.
Check that pairwise comparison does not change what counts as a correct critique.
Check whether Wen et al. refer to Saunders et al.'s critique tasks elsewhere.
out.other_title: Critique, critiqueability, helpfulness and conditional refinement tasks
out.rationale: Saunders et al. define a critique task (point out a flaw in an answer) plus critiqueability and helpfulness discrimination tasks. Wen et al. define a hierarchy from response to first-order critique to critique of critique (C2) and higher orders, using pairwise comparisons at each critique level; the cited Wen et al. passage cites standard RLHF practice (Ouyang et al., 2022) and does not refer to Saunders et al., so it does not show that Wen et al. build on Saunders et al.'s tasks.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: how to set up critique-based tasks for judging answers and critiques, which Saunders et al. do with a critique task and critiqueability and helpfulness discrimination tasks, and Wen et al. separately with a hierarchy of critiques of critiques and higher orders

text: The authors define a hierarchical critique architecture that runs from an initial response through a first-order critique, a second-order critique of critique (C2), and higher-order critiques. Each level uses pairwise comparison, following standard RLHF practice, which they motivate by humans' advantage in relative over absolute assessment and by consistency with the pairwise preference data needed for reward-model training in the AI experiments.
title: Recursive critique chain: response, critique, critique of critique (C2), higher orders
